_meta.indication: Treatment of candidemia and invasive candidiasis in patients 18 years of age or older who have limited or no alternative options; approval based on limited clinical safety and efficacy data.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled noninferiority study; 1:1 randomization to rezafungin vs caspofungin (with optional step-down to oral fluconazole in the caspofungin arm), with a 20% NI margin.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years of age with ≥1 systemic sign attributable to candidemia or invasive candidiasis seeking to treat this infection.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: All-cause mortality at Day 30 (prespecified primary endpoint).
pivotal_trials.n: 199 randomized (ITT); 187 in mITT population (rezafungin N=93, caspofungin N=94).
pivotal_trials.result: Study met primary endpoint: Day 30 all-cause mortality 23.7% (rezafungin) vs 21.3% (caspofungin), treatment difference 2.4% (95% CI -9.7%, 14.4%), within the 20% NI margin.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) included hypokalemia (15%), pyrexia (12%), diarrhea (11%), anemia (10%), vomiting (9%) and nausea (9%). A neurotoxicity signal (tremors) was noted: tremors occurred in 4/151 (2.6%) rezafungin-treated patients vs none with caspofungin.
target_moa: Rezafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin that inhibits the 1,3-β-D-glucan synthase enzyme complex, blocking synthesis of 1,3-β-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall not present in mammalian cells.

advisory_committee.vote: Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee convened January 24, 2023; voted 14 “yes”, 1 “no”, 0 abstentions on whether the benefit-risk assessment is favorable for treatment of candidemia/IC in adults with limited or no alternative treatment options.

basis.text: Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation granted June 27, 2017 for treatment of candidemia and invasive candidiasis.

citations.quote: On June 27, 2017, the same product was granted both QIDP and Fast Track designations for the requested indications.

summary.text: Rezafungin was developed for candidemia/invasive candidiasis with orphan drug designation (2016) and QIDP plus Fast Track designations (June 27, 2017), and the NDA was reviewed under priority review as a new molecular entity with QIDP designation. It was a full (traditional) approval based on a single phase 3 noninferiority study (ReSTORE), and was discussed at the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee.

citations.quote: In 2016, rezafungin was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of candidemia and invasive candidiasis caused by susceptible *Candida* species.
On June 27, 2017, the same product was granted both QIDP and Fast Track designations for the requested indications.

This NDA contains a single adequate and well-controlled phase 3 noninferiority (NI) study (ReSTORE) in adult subjects with candidemia/IC comparing IV rezafungin (REZ) to IV caspofungin (with optional stepdown to oral fluconazole in the caspofungin arm).

requirement.text: 4416-1: Conduct a United States surveillance study for a five-year period after introduction of rezafungin to the market to monitor changes in susceptibility of Candida species to rezafungin.
